title: The Goatherd and the Goat
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Goatherd was one day gathering his flock to return to the fold, when one of his goats strayed and refused to join the rest. He tried for a long time to get her to return by calling and whistling to her, but the Goat took no notice of him at all; so at last he threw a stone at her and broke one of her horns. In dismay, he begged her not to tell his master: but she replied, "You silly fellow, my horn would cry aloud even if I held my tongue." It's no use trying to hide what can't be hidden.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Goatherd doing when one of his goats strayed?
options: Milking his flock
Gathering his flock to return to the fold
Shearing his goats
Leading his flock to a new pasture

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Goatherd first try to get the Goat to return?
options: By offering her food
By calling and whistling to her
By chasing her with a stick
By sending another goat after her

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Goatherd do after the Goat ignored him?
options: He gave up and went home without her
He threw a stone at her and broke one of her horns
He asked a neighbor for help
He waited quietly for her to return on her own

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Goatherd beg the Goat to do?
options: Forgive him for his temper
Not tell his master
Return to the flock at once
Keep away from the other goats

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Goat call the Goatherd when she replies?
options: "My poor friend"
"You silly fellow"
"You cruel master"
"My careless keeper"

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "strayed" mean in "one of his goats strayed and refused to join the rest"?
options: Fell asleep
Wandered away from the group
Grew ill suddenly
Gave birth

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Goat mean by "my horn would cry aloud even if I held my tongue"?
options: Her broken horn will visibly reveal what happened even if she says nothing
She plans to tell the master herself out of spite
Her horn will heal before the master notices
She intends to warn the other goats about the Goatherd

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable's closing line?
options: Silence is always the safest choice after a mistake
Evidence of a wrongdoing can expose it even without anyone speaking a word
Goats are naturally more honest than their keepers
It is unwise to ever ask forgiveness for an accident

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Goat refuse to do at first?
options: Eat with the other goats
Join the rest of the flock
Drink from the stream
Follow the Goatherd's whistle command immediately

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Goat respond to the Goatherd's calling and whistling?
options: She took no notice of him at all
She came back immediately
She bleated loudly in reply
She led the rest of the flock away

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what part of the Goat did the stone break?
options: One of her legs
One of her horns
Her tail
Her ear

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "dismay" mean in "In dismay, he begged her not to tell his master"?
options: Great joy
Distress or alarm
Boredom
Confidence

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Goatherd's plea to keep quiet fail to matter?
options: The Goat plans to tell the master out of revenge
The visible injury to the Goat's horn will reveal the truth regardless of whether she says anything
The master already saw the Goatherd throw the stone
The other goats will surely report what happened

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Goatherd injures a stray Goat with a thrown stone, and she points out that the visible wound will betray him no matter what he asks of her
A Goatherd's goat runs away and is never found
A Goat forgives the Goatherd and promises never to stray again
A Goatherd is punished by his master before the Goat can say anything
